item.description: PISCATAWAY, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 29: Kaytron Allen #13 of the Penn State Nittany Lions runs with the ball against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights during the first half at SHI Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Rutgers football is set to kick off against Penn State this Saturday at 3:30 pm in Happy Valley. Earlier this week, I had the opportunity to catch up with Brian Bennett of SB Nation’s Penn State site, blackshoediaries.com, to ask him about his thoughts on this game and the Nittany Lions season so far. 1. How has Matt Campbell adjusted to his new role in Happy Valley, and what does the fanbase think about this season so far? I think there’s been a learning curve for Campbell at Penn State. It’s just a different game playing in the Big Ten than in the Big XII when it comes to not only the talent on the field, but the expectations, media coverage, etc. He was super conservative in some early season games and it bit the Lions in home losses to Wisconsin and USC. Most on our staff looked at the schedule and thought this team should go at least 8-4/9-3. They still might get to 8-4, but there has certainly been some frustration. The schedule was light – Penn State didn’t play Oregon or Ohio State or Indiana. I think there was some hope that this team could follow the same template Curt Cignetti did at IU (bring over a bunch of guys familiar with the program, take advantage of an easy schedule, slide into the playoff and build some momentum). That was dashed when they blew a 17-point lead against Wisconsin. Then there were losses to Michigan and USC where the Lions led in the second half, too. 2. How has Rocco Becht adjusted over the course of his first season in the Big Ten? He’s been, for lack of a better term, “fine”. Becht was a hero in Ames. He’s just been a stopgap at Penn State. The Nittany Lions are 6-4, possibly on their way to 8-4, and there’s been no “Rocco moment” at all. In fact, he’s been the inverse of clutch. His three turnovers led to all three touchdowns for Michigan in a narrow loss in the Big House. Wisconsin’s rally was sparked by him missing a few throws and throwing a key interception. He hasn’t been good enough to elevate Penn State at any point in the year, but he’s also been solid in stretches where the team has been at its best – most notably in the first half at Washington. 3. item.title: Barcelona duo Ebrima Tunkara and Jordi Pesquer star as Spain’s Under-17s win World Cup opener
item.description: DOHA, QATAR - NOVEMBER 20: Ebrima Tunkara celebrates with Junior Zamorano of Spain after scoring his team’s second goal during the FIFA U-17 World Cup Qatar 2026 match between Spain and China PR at the Aspire Zone on November 20, 2026 in Doha, Qatar. (Photo by Lewis Storey - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images) | FIFA via Getty Images Barcelona starlets Ebrima Tunkara and Jordi Pesquer shone as Spain’s Under-17s won their first game of the World Cup campaign on Friday. Tunkara was named in the starting XI for the match against China alongside Pesquer and Barcelona team-mates Sergi Mayans and Roberto Tomás. ¡Este es nuestro primer 𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗘 del #U17WC ! 🇪🇸 – 🇨🇳 📺 @teledeporte y @rtveplay #NuestraBase pic.twitter.com/hVClsVzyv9 — Selección Española Masculina de Fútbol (@SEFutbol) November 20, 2026 Pesquer gave Spain the lead five minutes before half-time from the penalty spot. The left-back won the spot kick and dusted himself off to take it, sweeping the ball low and into the far corner to make it 1-0. Tunkara then doubled Spain’s lead in stoppage time at the end of the first half with a simply wonderful free-kick. The teenager guided the ball over the wall and past the dive of the goalkeeper to open his account for the tournament. GOOOOLAZO! Ebrima Tunkara scores with a great free-kick. 2-0 pic.twitter.com/rpwBKocx6G — ArsenKveFCB (@ArsenKveFCB) November 20, 2026 The Barcelona star was involved again as Spain made it 3-0 on 74 minutes. Tunkara shrugged off a couple of challenges inside his own half before powering forwards and laying the ball off to Owen Emeka out wide on the right. Emeka then drove into the area and fired the ball home from the angle to finish the game as a contest. Yet Spain were celebrating again five minutes later when Emeka grabbed his second of the match. Pesquer, who also enjoyed a great game, did well to get forward and fire a low shot goalwards. Jordi Pesquer’s shot leads to 4-0 for Spain U17. Sensational game by the young left-back. pic.twitter.com/g3bAnZoYoe — ArsenKveFCB (@ArsenKveFCB) November 20, 2026 China goalkeeper Jiang Yuhan could only parry the ball into Emeka’s path and the youngster had the simple task of tapping home from close range to make it 4-0. Spain wrapped up a great start with a fifth and final goal on 85 minutes which saw more Barcelona involvement. Substitute Iu Martinez fizzed in a delicious low cross from the right for Guillermo Trujillano to sweep home and seal an emphatic victory.

item.title: New Sheriff in Town: Michigan’s Whittingham on the Hot Seat?
item.description: Nov 14, 2026; Eugene, Oregon, USA; Michigan Wolverines head coach Kyle Whittingham watches the replay monitor during the second half in a game against the Oregon Ducks at Autzen Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images Trev Alberts is heading to Ann Arbor at a difficult moment for Michigan football. The incoming athletic director inherits a program struggling through a 5-5 season , and first-year head coach Kyle Whittingham is already facing questions about whether he will get another year. Alberts, who is leaving Texas A&M to become Michigan’s next athletic director, is expected to begin his new role on Dec. 1. His appointment comes as the Wolverines try to recover from a disappointing season and a turbulent period for the athletic department. Bruce Feldman of The Athletic suggested the timing could be concerning for Whittingham. Speaking to Yahoo Sports, Feldman said that having a new athletic director in place before Thanksgiving is “probably bad news for Kyle Whittingham.” That comment reflects the growing uncertainty around the program, but Michigan has not announced any plans to replace its head coach. Michigan’s New Athletic Director Inherits a Difficult Situation Alberts replaces Warde Manuel , who announced in July that he would step down at the end of 2026. Manuel had served as Michigan’s athletic director since 2016, overseeing a period that included the football program’s national championship and several major controversies. The university moved quickly to secure Alberts, with incoming president C. Cybele Raver calling an emergency meeting of the Board of Regents to address the appointment. Alberts will have an opportunity to evaluate the athletic department as he takes over. His background includes athletic director roles at Nebraska and Texas A&M. At Nebraska, he made a major football decision in 2022, dismissing head coach Scott Frost midseason. Alberts subsequently hired Matt Rhule, who took over before the 2023 campaign. However, Alberts’ experience at Texas A&M offers an important distinction. He did not hire current Aggies head coach Mike Elko. Elko was already in place when Alberts arrived in College Station in March 2024. The new Michigan athletic director will have to determine whether Whittingham is the right person to lead the Wolverines forward. Whittingham Has Two Games to Change the Conversation Michigan’s record tells only part of the story. The Wolverines have lost five games, including defeats against Iowa, Minnesota, Michigan State, Oregon, and Indiana. Their offense has struggled to produce consistently, and Whittingham has already made a major staff change by dismissing offensive coordinator Jason Beck. The 31-7 loss to Oregon was particularly concerning. Michigan managed just seven points, continuing an offensive problem that has followed the team through much of the season. item.title: Filming training by drones should be illegal - Iraola
item.description: Andoni Iraola's Liverpool take on Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United on Sunday [Getty Images] Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola says filming with drones around training grounds should be illegal after Mauricio Pochettino's first session as Manchester United boss was captured and uploaded online. Pochettino and his players were clearly visible in the footage, which was shot above United's Carrington training base from a variety of angles and distances. The drone operater apologised and later took down the footage, with sources telling BBC Sport they are adamant there was no security breach and that they do not intend to take legal action. Iraola said he was sent the 12 minutes of footage on Thursday - three days before United travel to Anfield for a Premier League match. "The important part of this is that it shouldn't be legal," he said on Friday. "It happened to United but it could happen to me. "Yesterday, when Sky Sports had access to our training and the cameras recorded 15-20 minutes, you know who trained and who didn't. "It's not the matter of the advantage. It's the fact that someone can do this. There's a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect. I don't think it's nice for any club." Ten outfield players were seen working directly with former United States boss Pochettino in the footage, though it seems unlikely they will all start Sunday's match. "We've faced each other and obviously he [Pochettino] has a lot of Premier League games behind him that we can look at," said Iraola. "We can look at games from the US but it's true that they have this small advantage that we don't have references to prepare, because they can go different ways that we honestly don't know right now." Iraola said he expected United to be "well prepared" as Pochettino's assistants travelled to England to work with the players before the Argentine arrived on Wednesday. "They have this advantage that we don't exactly know - or at least we don't have the references like we do against other opposition," he said. "Especially the beginning of the game will be important. We have to adapt to certain things. But we know the players very well." Liverpool are fourth in the table - 14 places ahead of United. But they have failed to beat the Red Devils at Anfield in each of the past three seasons, and have lost to Arsenal and Manchester City at home already in this campaign. "You don't find bigger games than this," said Iraola. "I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be a part of these games. "We have to acknowledge the importance of the game. There are a lot of ingredients. They have a new manager, new challenges for us. This is important for us in a lot of different ways. "We want to improve our form at home. We have been very good away but not good at home and the first chance we have is United on Sunday." Pochettino training session filmed by drone - what did we learn? item.description: RB Leipzig v Manchester City - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 - Getty Images Sport Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has called for a sense of perspective as his side prepares to return to Premier League action against Fulham. Following a dip in results before the international break, the Italian tactician is determined to shield his high-profile stars from mounting external pressure. Finding stability amid the noise Reflecting on the recent run of results, Maresca emphasised the need for a measured approach, particularly after a spectacular start to his first Premier League season in charge of City, which saw him guide the team to a record seven consecutive wins - the best start to a managerial reign in the competition's history. However, City suffered three defeats in their following matches before the international break , which ends with Saturday's home clash against Fulham. 'I think there is always a reason why you win a game or you lose a game, no doubt. But it is a matter of balance,' Maresca explained. 'We were not perfect at the beginning when we were winning games and we've not been so bad when we lost the last three games. So that's why it is a matter of finding the right balance between the two things. And again, with the new players, a new manager, it is part of the process.' Maresca is well aware that even the most successful seasons are rarely without obstacles. He reminded supporters that adversity is a natural ingredient in the hunt for silverware. 'In all of the season when you achieve something important, you also go through difficult moments. I was here in the Treble season and we had some bad moments. It is normal and it is part of the season to drop some points, even more when you start something new like in our case with a new manager, new players and everything has changed.' Standing by Donnarumma Individual scrutiny has intensified during the break, particularly regarding Gianluigi Donnarumma. The Italian goalkeeper endured a challenging period with the national team in the UEFA Nations League, notably committing a high-profile error that allowed France to take the lead in Italy's 3-1 victory, before conceding four goals against Belgium. He has also made several costly mistakes for Manchester City during the 2026-27 season, including an error against Aston Villa that allowed Nicolas Jackson to score, leaving his near post exposed against RB Leipzig as Ridle Baku found the net from a tight angle, and facing criticism for his performance in City's 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. Maresca offered a full defence of his number one , acknowledging the errors while pointing to his shot-stopping qualities. 'He has been good,' Maresca said of Donnarumma. item.title: Maresca says struggling Man City not distracted by 'noise' around club
item.description: Enzo Maresca's Manchester City have lost their past three Premier League matches (Darren Staples) Enzo Maresca insists his Manchester City players are not distracted by the "noise" around the club's financial-rules case as he seeks to end their losing run. City flew out of the blocks in the Premier League this season, winning their first seven games, but three straight defeats have left them six points behind leaders Arsenal. The 10-time English champions are still waiting to discover the extent of their punishment after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. The club have repeatedly denied wrongdoing and have appealed against the verdict. But Maresca said he did not believe the case was weighing on the minds of his third-placed team ahead of their match against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. "I don't think the players are thinking too much about that," he said, "If we want to relate the noise with the defeats, Villa away, I think we had so many chances... Brighton here, the keeper was the man of the match. "The Forest one (a 3-1 defeat), where Erling (Haaland) had the chance to (make it) 2-2. I don't think the players are focused on the noise." Maresca admitted his side needed to improve but said not everything was perfect even when they were winning. "Overall, we control the game almost every time," said the Italian. "There are moments when we don't control the game and it is a moment when we need to understand the reason why and to do better." The former Chelsea boss, who replaced Pep Guardiola in the close-season, pointed out that he had not been at City for long, stressing his focus is on the long term. "Probably you forget a little bit about the time we spent together," he said. "It is not a big time that we are together. That is why I can see that what we are working on every day is there. "This is a good thing, it is a nice feeling. Also, the work we are doing is helping the players to be better players and to be a better team. For me, it is just the beginning of something long." City can take heart from their eye-catching 20-game winning run against Fulham in all competitions. "I didn't know that it's 20 games, hopefully 21," said Maresca. "It's a long time and hopefully tomorrow we can continue winning games against them." jw/smg/pi

item.title: The tale of the Wolves fans who did not return from a world cup to be shown
item.description: The documentary follows the adventures of a group of Wolves fans who went to the Mexico World Cup in 1986 and never came back to the UK [Gary Allen] A screening of a documentary about a group of Wolves fans who went to the 1986 World Cup in Mexico and did not return to the Black Country will take place at the club. The group decided not to return to their Stourbridge and Lye homes after attending the global football spectacular, embarking on new lives in the US instead. Gary Allen, who settled in Atlanta and who pitched the documentary, said "Wolves called us and said 'would you like to do the first screening in the UK at the Molineux? And of course all being Wolves fans we said 'we'd love to'." Lost Down Mexico Way will be shown at Molineux on Friday evening, just one part of reunion gatherings this week. The stars of the documentary are referred to by their nicknames. As well as Allen, known as Adder, it features Rabbithead (Garry Hardwicke), Batesy (Stuart Bates), Arnie (David Arnold) and Texas Steve (Steve Dawson). After the World Cup and a brief jaunt to Belize, the gang flew to Dallas, Texas. Gary Allen, known as Adder, said "before you know it, there's 40 years gone" [Gary Allen] The group had lived in the Black Country all their lives before flying 5,000 miles to experience the 1986 tournament. Allen, who retired from running his own company last year, has previously said the "opportunity was the biggest thing for us", as he talked about the US. "I think back in 86... the job situation wasn't the best back then. "I'd just lost my job, [Margaret] Thatcher was in power, a few of the lads were just doing painting and whatever. "We'd all saved a bit of money and the idea was to go out there and do a few weeks and just travel. We just played it by ear really." Allen added once "we got there and enjoyed it, it just went from there and we all stayed and then more and more came over". "And before you know it, there's 40 years gone," he said. "So it was just a chance we took back in the day and luckily it's panned out well for us." Of those attending, a coach from Stourbridge was leaving on Friday afternoon "and about four or five carloads". "So we've got 80 [in] total that Wolves have given us tickets for, so it should be a good reunion," Allen added. Allen said he was looking forward to having a "good chat, good reminisce". "As you get older you can't do it. "So this is a one-off and it'll be the last time I see a lot of people, but it's gonna be great and we'll certainly make the most of it." item.title: Report Milan ready to sell Estupinan and Loftus-Cheek, loan young talent out
item.description: Report Milan ready to sell Estupinan and Loftus-Cheek, loan young talent out Milan are expected to sell Pervis Estupinan and Ruben Loftus-Cheek in the January transfer window, with Turkish and English clubs interested, while Francesco Camarda and Christian Comotto are heading on loan. The Rossoneri have stuttered so far this season and found significant differences between the first choice team’s performance and those who come in during squad rotation. This has prompted three defeats out of four Europa League games so far, and coach Ruben Amorim is reportedly ready to cut some players loose. Milan clear out dead wood JAKARTA, INDONESIA – AUGUST 08: Pervis Estupinan of AC Milan controls the ball against Pedro Neto of Chelsea FC during the pre-season friendly between Chelsea FC and AC Milan at Gelora Bung Karno Stadium on August 08, 2026 in Jakarta, Indonesia. (Photo by Peksi Cahyo/Getty Images) Amorim had declared at the start of the season that he convinced Milan to keep hold of Estupinan when a move to Aston Villa had been practically agreed. Now several months on, he seemingly regrets that decision and has given the all-clear for an exit, but the Premier League side is no longer interested. A loan move to Fiorentina could be on the cards , although they hope to find a more permanent solution to make back some of that investment. ITALY – SEPTEMBER 14: Ruben Loftus-Cheek of AC Milan in action during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Bologna FC 1909 at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on September 14, 2025 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Loftus-Cheek is only under contract with the Rossoneri until the end of this season, but persistent injuries and poor performances should see him sold in January. Coventry City had made an approach in the summer, and could well try again, but Besiktas and other Turkish teams are also options. Francesco Camarda scores from the penalty spot during a pre-season friendly between Celtic and Milan at Celtic Park (via www.acmilan.com) Meanwhile, young players Camarda and Comotto are clearly not going to get a chance to deliver, so will be sent out on loan in January to gain valuable experience. Genoa are the most advanced in talks for midfielder Comotto, while Camarda has numerous proposals from Serie A, B, and even abroad.

item.description: FILE PHOTO - USA manager and new Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino during press conference at the Arthur M. Blank National Training Centre. Pochettino has been appointed as Manchester United head coach from November 18, the club have announced. (is associated with: «Pochettino outlines his expectations in first Man Utd press conference») Press Association/PA Wire/dpa Mauricio Pochettino wants a say in “all the main decisions” around Manchester United’s squad after arriving as the club’s new head coach this week. Pochettino addressed the media for the first time as United boss on Friday, two days before the trip to face old rivals Liverpool – a match United will start inside the relegation zone. United’s recent recruitment has come in for heavy criticism with a feeling that Pochettino’s predecessor Michael Carrick was left short-handed by the club’s summer business, overseen by director of football Jason Wilcox. Geno Auriemma has spent over four decades turning UConn into the gold standard of college basketball. item.title: View From The Other Offseason – Ivan the Great of Battery Power
item.description: In 2025, the Braves finally seemed to right themselves after a couple of shaky years, winning their division despite a rash of injuries, especially to their starting pitching. However, even after winning their seventh division title in ten years, they ran into the Dodgers who managed to shutdown their bats and knock them out of the postseason in the NLDS 3-1. We talked to Ivan the Great of Battery Power about their takeaways from the 2026 season and what the Braves can look forward to in 2027. With the 2026 season in the rearview mirror, what do team fans think are the key takeaways, both good and bad on the season? I think this is one of those things where asking five Braves fans will give you seven opinions. On top of that, the Braves had a very strange 2026 season, which only makes the narrative more complicated. The good is that the Braves ended up where they were expected to be: lots of wins, on top of the division. There’s still clearly a fair bit of talent in the organization, and there are things the organization does really well, namely in major league pitching development. The bad is that 2026 was Year Two of “some component of the organization has no idea what to do offensively.” After a very specific offensive approach that we jokingly call “The PowerPoint” from 2019-2024, the Braves pivoted away from it hard in 2025 to disastrous results – and 2026 was a mixed bag of stuff that sometimes looked like 2019-2024, sometimes looked like 2025, and often just felt like flailing for a life preserver. Combine that with blow after blow of pitching injuries, and I think I’d probably list the takeaways as: 1) the team has a lot of good players; 2) the organization is for some reason unsure or incapable of getting the most out of those players on the hitting end; and, 3) the pitching health is always more dire than the organization seems to plan for, such that it’s an ongoing scramble for more arms that feels a bit like juggling chainsaws. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
